Long ago, when the world was young, there lived a river spirit named Celara who had never seen her own face. She knew every fish, every stone, every ripple in her waters, but her own reflection remained a mystery, for rivers cannot see themselves—they only flow.

One day, a wandering cloud named Aether descended to drink from her waters. "Why do you weep?" he asked, feeling her sadness.

"I know all things except myself," Celara replied.

Moved by her sorrow, Aether made a promise. He rose high into the sky and called upon the rain. For forty days and nights, he wept silver tears upon a distant mountain, filling a great crater with the purest water.

When the rains ceased, the crater became perfectly still—the world's first mirror lake. Aether led Celara's spirit there, and for the first time, she gazed upon her own shimmering form.

Overwhelmed with joy, Celara blessed the lake, declaring that all who looked into still waters would see not just their faces, but glimpses of their souls.

And that is why, even today, we seek our reflections in quiet pools—searching, like Celara, to know ourselves.
